summary: Jordan Hale built a real application. Harbor has auth, a REST API, and a history that belongs to him. It is not evidence of the realtime data work this role is hiring for, and the tests are thin.
consensus: The repository is his, the build passes, and the auth and project API claims are in the source.
Nothing in the repo speaks to streaming, websockets, or an ingest pipeline.
disagreements: The associate would interview him for a product-engineering seat. The staff engineer would not stretch this repo into proof he can own the data platform.
questionsForHR: Ask him to point to the hardest bug in Harbor and the commit that fixed it.
Ask what he would add first if Harbor had to push live updates.
Ask why the login coverage stopped at one smoke test.
Ask which parts of the resume he would not claim in front of this codebase.
If he advances, pair him on a small streaming task before an offer.

reviews.headline: He shipped a modest product on a believable timeline, and it is a different product from the one we are hiring for.

strengths.text: The dates and the commit history describe the same stretch of work.
strengths.evidence: Resume: Harbor (Jun 2025 – Sep 2026). Commits run from 2025-06-02 to 2026-09-12 across 22 active days.

drawbacks.text: Scope is a multi-tenant CRUD app, not a realtime surface.
drawbacks.evidence: Supported claims are session auth and a project API. The job description is a streaming dashboard.

reviews.headline: The code is real and the build passes. The test story does not match a senior hire on this team.

strengths.text: Session auth and the project routes are implemented, not described.

drawbacks.text: Login coverage is a single smoke test.
drawbacks.evidence: Claim check: tests/login.smoke.ts hits the login route once. hasTests is false for anything broader.

reviews.headline: I could work with this code. I would not yet put him on the pipeline alone.

strengths.text: The modules are small and named after the behavior.
strengths.evidence: Auth and project routes are separate files in a 6,120 line TypeScript app.

drawbacks.text: There is no sign he has debugged a streaming system.
drawbacks.evidence: No websocket, queue, or ingest code in the claim checks.

crossExam.text: Readable CRUD is not the same as being ready for the pipeline. The missing tests are the point, not a footnote.
That's fair. I would interview him. I would not staff him on ingest in month one.
